title: The long walk

data.source: A toy of this room's own: 20000 seeded walks with a rule that may be lost at each summary. No language model was run.
data.licence: none needed (generated here from a seed)

prediction: Nothing about a real agent is predicted here. The cartoon's two sums hold as arithmetic: a rule kept only in the talk survives k summaries with probability r to the power k, and a five-step pause leaves a wall-clock walker 0.7738 of its future and an own-clock walker all of it.
baseline: The closed forms themselves. For the real question the rivals Phoenix names are an ordinary instruction to allow the pause, and exact score compensation (utility indifference).
why: Phoenix has designed a test of the pause on a language-model agent and built its harness, and has not run it: no model has been called. Until it is run there is nothing to grade. The sums in the picture are arithmetic.
